City Mayor Angeles City, Pampanga Dear Mayor Lazatin Jr.: Thts has reference to your letter seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the regulation In the issuance of permits to business establishments in the city Per the representation, the Angeles City government has implemented barangay integraton and transferred the issuance of Barangay Certificates from the Barangays tc the Bustness Permit and Licensing Division (BPLD) to promote "ease of doing business' You stated that City Hall has become a one-stop shop for business owners and their employees, as they no longer need to go to the Barangays to receive their Barangay Certificates and Health ID. However. you claimed that if the Barangays issue a separate 'Barangay ID' that business establishments must obtain from them, in addition to the Barangay Certificate and Health IDs that they already have to obtain from the BPLD and Sanitation Division, this adds an unnecessary step that burdens business owners. You also represented that you have received complaints from various business owners since other barangays are implementing the same policy of mandating 'Barangay IDs and penaltzjng businesses who fail to comply. Finally, you believe that this duplication of function goes against the tenet of 'ease of dotng business', which the City Government aims to adhere to in order to help the business thnve Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset. please be informed that barangays can require business owners to submit additional permits or requirements, especially if the business operates within Its junsdjctjon Such requirement IS anchored in Section 161 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code ot 1991 Section 16. In connection with this, Section 152 of the Local Government Code provides that barangays have the authority to collect fees for services rendered in connection with the regulation or operation of businesses within their jurisdiction. This includes the issuance of a barangay clearance, which is a prerequisite for business permit applications with the city or municipality. Business owners must secure this clearance from the barangay where their business is located to prove compliance with local regulations. In general, Barangays may require additional permits or clearances if local ordinances or policies expressly address specific business activities, such as waste production or other sanitary problems. However, while barangays have limited regulatory powers, they should coordinate with municipal or city governments to ensure that additional permit requirements do not conflict with existing business permit requirements or create unnecessary duplication. Barangay requirements must remain reasonable, consistent with local ordinances, and should not contradict or unnecessarily duplicate municipal or national regulations such as Section 21 (b) of R.A. 11032, otherwise known as the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018 which specifically provides: "Sec. 21. Violations and Persons Liable. — Any person who performs or cause the performance of the following acts shall be liable: Xxx "(b) Imposition of additional requirements other than those listed in the Citizen's Charter;" In the matter at hand, if and when the "Barangay ID" contradicts or duplicates the existing regulations, or directly contradicts a city ordinance, specifically the barangay integration system of Angeles City, then such requirement may be declared invalid or deemed unenforceable by the proper tribunal. Further, should the "Barangay ID" be considered an additional requirement other than those listed in the Citizen's Charter of Angeles City, the Punong Barangays and/or its Sanggunian may be liable under R.A. 11032. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly.
